bug_semantics: With federation enabled, NodeBB authenticated the HTTP-signature key against the ActivityPub activity actor and required object.id to have that actor's origin, but did not bind object.attributedTo to the authenticated actor. A remote actor could therefore send a signed Create whose object.id was on the attacker's origin but whose attributedTo was a bare local numeric uid such as 1. The inbound mock copied attributedTo into the post/message uid; actors.assert filtered numeric identifiers out and its false result was ignored, after which topic or chat persistence treated the attacker-chosen local uid as the author.
flaw_origin: Commit f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 first made the unsafe attribution mapping remotely exploitable: it added inbox.create, took only req.body.object for authorship, passed the untrusted object through activitypub.mocks.post, and persisted the resulting postData without comparing attributedTo to the authenticated req.body.actor. The unsafe mocks.post assignment had been prepared in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 and moved by 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, but f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the smallest commit that connected it to the inbound Create attack surface and made the remote post-forgery path real.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` shows human author and committer Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>, the message `feat: handle Create(note)`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8m27-grg5-27vj and its referenced vulnerable tree https://github.com/NodeBB/NodeBB/blob/v4.13.2/src/activitypub/mocks.js describe the unsigned-author binding failure and the bare numeric attributedTo local-uid exploit.

`git show f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 -- src/activitypub/inbox.js` adds inbox.create: it reads object from req.body, calls activitypub.mocks.post(object), and sends postData to activitypub.notes.assert without reading or comparing the authenticated actor. The commit has one parent, so it is neither a merge nor a squash aggregate.

Direct parent-tree verification with `git grep -n 'inbox.create = async' 756548520401e1f920d358ad61ec1f28451173d5 -- src/activitypub/inbox.js` returned no match. The parent already contained the generic mock, but no inbound Create handler connected a remote signed activity to that mock-and-persist path; the f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 diff is the minimal enabling change.

At v4.13.2, src/middleware/activitypub.js verifies the HTTP signature, derives req.uid from keyId, checks key ownership against req.body.actor, and checks actor hostname against object.id hostname, but never checks object.attributedTo. src/activitypub/inbox.js create passes object to notes.assert; src/activitypub/mocks.js maps attributedTo to uid, calls actors.assert(uid) without checking its return, and returns uid in the persistence payload; src/activitypub/actors.js explicitly filters numeric ids; src/activitypub/notes.js ultimately calls topics.post with authorId or messaging.sendMessage with payload.uid.

History cross-checks show the precursor assignment `attributedTo: uid` originated in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458, was only moved by refactor 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, and became remotely reachable in f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7. Later d948334713dc0857c28ec680f935e16e293bb73a added the ignored actors.assert(uid) call, and 4ec7552cfbbdf23c6f51b905e2e1536777695b70 added normalization/private-message mocking, expanding but not originating the flaw.

`git tag --contains f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7` includes v4.0.0-alpha, every stable v4 release through the vulnerable v4.13.2, and later descendants; `git merge-base --is-ancestor f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 v3.12.9` exits 1. Thus the boundary is the v4 ActivityPub line, with v3.12.9 outside this BIC's ancestry.

Direct fix dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35 adds `if (!activitypub.helpers.isUri(attributedTo)) throw` in src/activitypub/mocks.js and states that the guard prevents a number from enabling unchecked impersonation of local users. Its parent b799d51d9b513a121fa9ba7204a0e7b764dea284 lacks that guard. `git tag --contains dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35` starts at v4.14.0, whereas v4.13.2 predates it; this establishes the vulnerable/patched release boundary for the advisory's local-uid vector. Follow-up f93507a6404ce0e32e6e7befb47ef3a1f56bbac1 additionally enforces attributedTo origin matching in Create/Update handlers.

BIC-only AI attribution comes from the raw f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 commit object: Julian Lam is both author and committer and there are no trailers or bot markers. No later fix or refactor signal is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The causal split matters. f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 created a generic remote-note mock that trusted attributedTo, but its existence alone did not provide the advisory's unauthenticated remote inbox attack. f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the first complete vulnerable state: it added the signed inbound Create handler and connected the untrusted object to that mock and persistence while omitting the authenticated actor from the author decision. Its immediate parent has no inbox.create handler, so the remote path is directly absent there. Subsequent commits moved and broadened the implementation, including a numeric-id filter whose failure was ignored and a private-message path, but those are not smaller origins. The BIC precedes v4.0.0-alpha and is present in v4.13.2; dc45bd7f98168e8c5726e36a8f84a519cc2dbc35 blocks the exact bare-number local-user impersonation vector and first ships in v4.14.0. Because the only admissible AI evidence is the BIC commit object and that object is a trailer-free human commit, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
